html:
The Hindu Shahis ruled Kabul, Gandhara and the Punjab from about 822 to 1026. On the 900 map they hold the land between Kabul and the Punjab rivers.

They took power from the Buddhist Turk Shahis when a minister, Kalarapala, overthrew the last Turk Shahi king. His successor lost Kabul to the Saffarids, and the capital moved east to Udabhandapura, on the Indus. Their silver coins, with a bull and a horseman, were copied across the region.

From the 10th century they faced the Turks of Ghazni. Jayapala lost to Sabuktigin, and in 1001 to Mahmud of Ghazni near Peshawar; he then burned himself to death in shame. His son Anandapala and grandson Trilochanapala kept fighting, but the Ghaznavids had swallowed their kingdom by 1026. The scholar Al-Biruni praised them as noble kings.
sum: The Hindu Shahis ruled Kabul, Gandhara and the Punjab from about 822 to 1026. On the 900 map they hold the land between Kabul and the Punjab rivers.
